_comment: WEMOS LOLIN C3 PICO — project-local board definition.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: platform espressif32 7.0.1 ships lolin_c3_mini but
no lolin_c3_pico, and the pinned Arduino core (2.0.17) has no
variants/lolin_c3_pico either. Upstream added both in arduino-esp32 3.x.
PlatformIO reads boards/ in the project root, so the board can be named
correctly here without waiting for the core bump.
WHY variant lolin_c3_mini: the two boards have the SAME pin map. Compared
against upstream variants/lolin_c3_pico/pins_arduino.h and the
CircuitPython board definitions, both give SDA=8, SCL=10, RGB LED=7,
RX=20, TX=21, SCK=1, MISO=0, MOSI=4, SS=5, A0..A5=GPIO0..5. They differ
in form factor and connectors (the PICO has JST battery + LOLIN I2C, the
Mini has the shield header), which no variant header describes.
WHEN THE CORE IS UPGRADED to arduino-esp32 3.x: set variant to
lolin_c3_pico, or delete this file and use the platform's own board id.
Check the pin map still matches before doing either.
ARDUINO_LOLIN_C3_MINI is deliberately kept alongside the PICO macro: the
variant is the Mini's, so code that keys off the board macro should see
the board whose pins_arduino.h it actually got. Nothing in this project
keys off either (USB pin locking keys off the chip family instead — see
src/modules/UsbCdcModule.cpp).
NO -DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT HERE, unlike lolin_c3_mini.json upstream.
The env sets it, and the deploy tool rewrites it there; a copy in the
board definition means every unit compiles with a GCC macro-redefinition
warning the moment the two disagree, which is exactly when the toggle is
used. ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1 stays: nothing toggles it.
hwids use a LOWERCASE 0x prefix. PlatformIO's normalize_board_hwid()
(device/finder.py) does .replace("0x", "") and only then .upper(), so an
upstream-style "0X303A" never matches a detected port and `pio run -t
upload` falls back to guessing the last USB device. lolin_c3_mini.json
has the capital-X form; this does not.
